resolved_findings.finding: A single NSpid field, full UID map and equality with namespace-local PID 1 did not prove initial PID namespace; private procfs could hide host consumers.
resolved_findings.resolution: Require pinned kernel release and held nsfs descriptor identity/type; initial PID/user namespace inodes fixed to pinned vendor kernel definitions. Retain PID 1 equality and secondary status checks.

checks: Exact model/serial/capacity, 512/512 sectors, namespace and p1-p5 node identity/sysfs topology, partition geometry and ioctl geometry/RO checks bind the known target. All geometry/GPT pins agree with retained construction manifest.

Only p1 is opened writable, with O_EXCL and nonblocking exclusive flock; whole namespace descriptor is read-only. Exact p1 bounded copying cannot address GPT or p2-p5, and GPT hashes are independently checked before/after and immediately before application.

Held source descriptor is fully SHA-256 authenticated before writable target admission; protected root0600 single-link tmpfs source and root0700 parent metadata/path/identity are rechecked before and after streaming. Trusted quiescent root is an explicit procedural assumption.

Target remains held during export and application. Namespace, target identity and idle checks repeat; all visible threads are inspected for mount namespaces, descriptors, cwd/root/exe and maps; swap and holders are rejected. Unexpected census access failures are fatal.

Export copies live p1 read-only, fsyncs RAM output and fully authenticates OLD_SHA256. Apply/rollback require exact caller-pinned receipt hash, root0600 receipt metadata, serial/size/old-hash/current-boot binding and positive remote verification assertion. Receipt authentication depends explicitly on trusted control-channel pin delivery.

Forward old-to-new and reverse new-to-old predecessor checks, progress, short-write handling, exact 512MiB bound, fsync/BLKFLSBUF and optional readback are consistent. Failure reports conservatively use null bytes_written after apply admission.
